messages:
pagerbot: INCIDENT: latency-slo routing oscillation detected for service managed-api (eu). p95 spiked > 2.0s, auto-reroute engaged repeatedly -> high churn. Paging on-call.

jessica: taking pager, ack. joining from phone. will get runbook up. :rotating_light:

sam: i'm on the routing nodes, pulling recent decisions. headroom looks fine, this is policy churn not capacity.

sam: recent flips (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z route -> eu-central-1 model=v1-stable (p95 1.1s)
2026-03-15T02:13:09Z SLO_TRIGGER -> reroute -> eu-west-1 model=v1-quant (p95 2.6s)
2026-03-15T02:13:55Z route -> eu-central-1 model=v1-stable (p95 1.2s)
2026-03-15T02:14:40Z SLO_TRIGGER -> reroute -> eu-west-1 model=v1-quant (p95 3.0s)
```

anya: hmm, the fallback selector is preferring the "v1-quant" variant in eu-west-1 when latency SLOs hit. that variant was added to the fallback pool yesterday to save cost, but it has slower cold-paths for long-context requests. looks like the selector has too-low hysteresis and no model-quality check.

leo: confirmed — model metadata has fallback.allowed=true for v1-quant and compatible_tags include "latest" incorrectly. snippet from model-catalog: 
```
model: v1-quant
fallback: true
compatible: ["latest"]  # should be ["compact","low-latency"]
```
-> means fallback matched across contexts it shouldn't.

jessica: mitigation plan: 1) disable auto-reroute for this policy (latency-slo) for 10m, 2) pin traffic to v1-stable in eu-central-1, 3) remove v1-quant from fallback pool for eu region, 4) open follow-up bug for catalog tag fix. anyone object?

sam: +1. preparing router changes.

sam: executing now:
```
# disable auto reroute for latency-slo policy
routerctl policy update latency-slo --auto-reroute=false --hysteresis-ms=120000
# pin route for managed-api -> eu-central-1:v1-stable
routerctl route pin managed-api eu-central-1 v1-stable --duration=30m
# remove v1-quant from fallback pool in eu
modelctl set-fallback v1-quant --region eu --enabled=false
```

sam: routerctl: OK. route pin applied. modelctl: OK. changes propagated to control plane.

pagerbot: EVENT: manual override applied by sam — auto-reroute disabled, traffic pinned. Incident note: override_id=or-20260315-01.

matt: customer-impact: 3 mid-market tenants in EU saw elevated p95 (~2-3s) from 02:12-02:20 UTC. roughly 1.8k requests affected total. customers notified via status page; no data/exfil concerns.

anya: metrics: p95 dropped back under 1.3s after pinning and removing fallback. graphs look stable for last 6m.

jessica: good. i'm handing to tomas for follow-up and RCA. i'll stay available for 15m then hand off. paging: @tomas you're up for postmortem. :busts_in_silhouette:

pagerbot: PAGE: tomas — on-call transfer scheduled now (15min handoff).

tomas: taking handoff, thanks team. I'll open an RCA ticket (RCA-2026-03-15-01) and link runbook. schedule: deep-dive in 48h, assign eng-runtime + ml-ops.

jessica: summary for postmortem: root cause = fallback model-tag mismatch + too-aggressive reroute hysteresis leading to oscillation; impact = transient p95 breaches for a subset of EU tenants; mitigation = manual disable + pin + remove variant; next actions = catalog tag fix, add model-compat checks to selector, increase default hysteresis for latency SLO policies.

sam: adding config diffs to incident ticket and exporting routing logs.

matt: status page updated, customers will get follow-up email w/ RCA link.

tomas: ack. leaving manual controls with sam/anya for 30m, will reopen auto-reroute once we've validated 60m of stability.

jessica: thanks all. closing pager, will update incident ticket with timeline and handoff notes. :white_check_mark:

References: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-routing-oscillation, ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RCA-2026-03-15-01
